question: Can a parent-preserving policy-improvement teacher avoid equal-return imitation damage and improve whole-run decisions on the same data?
evidence: E157:6213/7448 branch states have equal tau values; their old imitation target suppresses the initial parent logit. Strict observed-maximum improvement is available at449 states, while tau marks658. E156 changes98/128 natural paths and wins7 versus parent13.
teacher: On the exact existing transition DAG, compute recorded-action optimal terminal returns. At each full state, retain the deterministic parent if its action attains that maximum. Otherwise give uniform categorical probability to recorded maximizing alternatives. The teacher differs from the parent at449 of7448 branch states; every single-action state retains its parent. No hidden state identity or return is an input to the neural actor.
objective: Unweighted full-menu categorical cross entropy to that target; tied failures and tied wins teach the parent. Replace the entire E156 advantage-weighted imitation target. This intentionally changes both the continuation reference (observed maximum) and parent-preserving tie behavior; it is a coherent policy-improvement target test, not an isolated estimate of either change.

specific_target_repair_benefit: Against E156 exact-weight actor require net>=4/128,p<.05; separately require parent net>=8,p<.025 to qualify for the next stage. Historical adaptive development evidence is not final unseen acceptance.
